title: Allen 01 pili: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: Allen 01 pili: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Allen 01 pili is a pili variety from Jose Agbon Bacuetes. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Allen 01 is a registered pili variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2008 as NSIC 2008 Pl 10. Jose Agbon Bacuetes bred it. Its record notes a yield of 7,500 pcs/harvest.

heroImage.alt: Young fruit trees planted in straight rows on cleared red soil, the kind of farm where Allen 01 pili is grown

blocks.text: The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry. Compare it with the others in our [pili variety finder](/crop-varieties/pili), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).
When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Allen 01 was about 45 years old and about 18 meters tall when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 7,500 pcs/harvest. It bears every year, with fruit in March May (peak fruiting). A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.
A fruit of Allen 01 weighs about 46.87 grams, and its shape is oblong. The flesh is black. The registry notes its fruiting season as March May (peak fruiting), bearing annual.
Where and when to plant Allen 01 pili

Bicol grows most of the pili. Pick a registered selection by kernel weight and the share of kernel in the nut, and plant grafted trees, because seedlings can turn out male. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.a: The record shows a recorded yield of 7,500 pcs/harvest. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Allen 01?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
